question.question: Does an acceptor that admits and acknowledges Accept retain phase/value history sufficient for subsequent Prepare-based recovery to preserve that accepted command and ordering tuple?
question.importance: If acknowledged acceptance is later treated as only preacceptance or no value, recovery could choose incompatible commands or dependencies after coordinator failure; this is a potential consensus-safety consequence, not an observed violation.
objects: One instance and its command/sequence/dependency tuple
contexts: Fixed odd membership with normal f=(N-1)/2 and Thrifty enabled
Non-durable operation without crash-restart; coordinator crash or delayed messages may initiate recovery

question.trigger_rationale: S_accept assigns bal/vbal/Seq/Deps but leaves Status unchanged; S_prepare exports that Status, and S_recover_select treats ACCEPTED differently from PREACCEPTED/NONE. This is an actual producer/consumer discrepancy worth a small legal-history experiment. Before a costly cluster test, reconstruct a generated Accept and its Prepare response; a separate metadata discrepancy has weaker deployment applicability.

candidate.rationale: Fix the local acceptance-history obligation for the existing question; global outcome remains unresolved.

obligation.description: After an acceptor admits an Accept for an existing uncommitted instance and acknowledges that request at its ballot, a subsequent successful higher-ballot Prepare must report that instance as ACCEPTED if no intervening protocol action has replaced its value or advanced its phase. This preserves the accepted-versus-preaccepted distinction required by recovery selection.

scope.description: Local acceptance-phase history exported by PrepareReply after admitted acceptance; no intervening value/phase change for the same instance.
assumptions: Fixed non-Byzantine membership; requests are emitted by actual protocol producers.
No crash/restart or durable-store recovery in this history.
No concurrent mutation while a handler or its serialized reply is observed.
excluded: Full-cluster agreement or application output divergence
Whether subsequent recovery actually selects a different tuple
Promise/value-ballot wire preservation as a separate responsibility
Automatic recovery timing or eventual completion

grounding.derivation: This is a local phase-history interface obligation, derived from the actual consumer rather than from the EPaxos name. The coordinator counts a matching-ballot AcceptReply as acceptance support (S_accept_reply). PrepareReply exposes Status as the phase of the retained value (S_wire, S_prepare). Recovery explicitly gives ACCEPTED a preservation branch before preacceptance/restart (S_recover_select 1228-1235,1255-1312), and S_try 1357-1360 states accepted history must not regress to preaccepted. Therefore an admitted and acknowledged Accept must establish acceptance that a later Prepare can recognize, absent an intervening value-changing request or decision. bal/vbal alone cannot substitute for Status at this consumer because its branch tests Status. This requirement concerns one acceptor report, not whether a quorum eventually decides a different value.
grounding.applicability: Initialized fixed-membership EPaxos acceptor, non-durable operation, existing uncommitted command and admitted Accept with matching acknowledgment. No intervening request changes that same instance value/phase; next Prepare has a greater ballot. Independent instances may progress.
unresolved: No separate protocol specification is used; applicability rests on the internal acceptance and recovery interface semantics.
The local report discrepancy alone does not establish a global agreement violation.
alternatives: The original coordinator retains ACCEPTED status and other replicas could preserve the value during recovery.
Command and ordering fields may remain intact even if phase reporting fails.
